grammar.title: Formal future forms
grammar.explanation_pt:
**1. Previsões (jornalismo, relatórios):**
- **be set to** + verbo: muito provável, já encaminhado — "Renewables **are set to** overtake coal."
- **be expected / likely / predicted to**: "Temperatures **are expected to** rise by..."
- **be poised to**: pronto para agir, prestes a — "The country **is poised to** become a leader in green hydrogen."
- **be bound to**: certeza (revisão C1-M2)

**2. Iminência:**
- **be about to** + verbo: prestes a (muito em breve) — "The meeting **is about to** start."
- **be on the verge / point / brink of** + substantivo ou -ing: à beira de
  "on the **verge of** a breakthrough" / "on the **point of** leaving" / "on the **brink of** extinction" (brink = algo negativo, catastrófico)

**3. Horários e cronogramas:**
- **be due to** + verbo / **be due** + tempo: previsto para — "The report **is due to** be published in May." / "The train **is due** at 5."

**4. be to + verbo** (formal): planos oficiais, ordens, instruções, destino
- Plano oficial: "The summit **is to be held** in Belém." / "The president **is to visit** the Amazon."
- Ordem/instrução: "You **are to report** to the director immediately." / "All staff **are not to** leave the building."
- Em condicionais: "If we **are to** meet our targets, we must act now." (= se quisermos)
- Passado (destino): "He **was** never **to** see his homeland again." (nunca mais veria)

**5. Futuro no passado** (revisão): was going to / was about to / was to have + pp (plano frustrado: "The bridge **was to have opened** in 2020.")

**Manchetes:** omitem o **be**: "Emissions **set to** fall" / "PM **to** resign" / "Species **on brink of** extinction".

rows: The film is about to start.
The plane is due to land at 8.

examples.en: Solar energy is set to become one of the main sources of electricity in Brazil within the next decade.
examples.pt: A energia solar deve se tornar uma das principais fontes de eletricidade do Brasil na próxima década.

examples.en: Scientists warn that parts of the Amazon could be approaching a tipping point, beyond which the forest might turn into savannah.
examples.pt: Cientistas alertam que partes da Amazônia podem estar se aproximando de um ponto de não retorno, além do qual a floresta poderia virar savana.

examples.pt: Se o mundo quiser limitar o aquecimento a 1,5°C, as emissões precisarão cair drasticamente nesta década.

grammar.tip_pt: **If we are to...** é uma estrutura poderosa em redações: "**If** Brazil **is to** meet its climate goals, deforestation must end." Significa "**se quisermos / para que**" — e mostra domínio C1.

pronunciation.tip_pt: Manchetes lidas em voz alta (no rádio, por exemplo) acentuam as palavras de conteúdo e quase "engolem" as gramaticais: "Emissions **SET** to **FALL**" / "Minister **TO** re**SIGN**". O **to** de "be to" é forte quando é a ideia principal.

dialogue.title: Covering the climate summit

lines.speaker: Bruno
lines.en: The big one: several countries are set to announce new emissions targets. Brazil is poised to present its plan for ending illegal deforestation.

lines.speaker: Editor

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.en: Here are today's climate headlines. Renewable energy is set to supply more than half of the country's electricity by the end of the decade, according to a new industry report. Wind and solar capacity are expected to keep growing rapidly, although experts warn that investment in transmission lines will be needed if the targets are to be met. Meanwhile, scientists say a species of frog found only in the Atlantic Forest is on the brink of extinction, following years of habitat loss. A rescue programme is to be launched next month. In the south of the country, farmers are on the verge of losing a second harvest to drought, and the government is due to announce emergency support on Friday. And finally, the city council is poised to approve a plan to plant one million trees, which, if successful, could make the city significantly cooler within twenty years.

reading.title: The Amazon at a tipping point?
reading.text: For decades, scientists have warned that the Amazon rainforest may be approaching a critical threshold. The concept is relatively simple. The forest generates a large share of its own rainfall: trees release moisture into the air, which forms clouds that carry rain further inland. As deforestation and climate change reduce the number of trees and increase temperatures, this cycle weakens. Beyond a certain point — a "tipping point" — parts of the forest could be unable to sustain themselves and might gradually turn into a drier, savannah-like ecosystem. Estimates of where exactly that point lies vary. In widely cited work, the Brazilian climate scientist Carlos Nobre and the American biologist Thomas Lovejoy suggested that it might be reached if deforestation exceeded around 20 to 25 percent of the original forest. Some studies indicate that parts of the eastern Amazon are already showing signs of stress, with longer dry seasons and, in certain areas, the forest releasing more carbon than it absorbs. Not all researchers agree on how close the tipping point is, and the forest is likely to respond differently from region to region. What is broadly accepted, however, is that the consequences of large-scale dieback would extend far beyond the Amazon itself. Rainfall in other parts of South America, including Brazil's agricultural heartland, depends partly on moisture from the forest. There are reasons for cautious hope. Deforestation rates have fallen significantly in some recent years, demonstrating that policy and enforcement can make a difference. Restoration projects are also under way. But if the Amazon is to remain a rainforest, many scientists argue, the next two decades are likely to be decisive.

questions.q: How does the Amazon generate its own rainfall?
questions.answer: Trees release moisture that forms clouds carrying rain further inland.

questions.q: What might happen beyond the tipping point?
questions.answer: Parts of the forest could turn into a drier, savannah-like ecosystem.

questions.q: What threshold did Nobre and Lovejoy suggest?
questions.answer: Around 20–25% deforestation of the original forest.

questions.q: Why would the consequences extend beyond the Amazon?
questions.answer: Rainfall elsewhere in South America, including farming regions, depends partly on the forest's moisture.

writing.model:
Coastal city set to build "sponge parks" to fight flooding

A coastal city in southern Brazil is set to become one of the first in the country to adopt "sponge city" techniques on a large scale, as it struggles to cope with increasingly frequent floods. (Fictional story created for this lesson.)

The city council is due to vote next Tuesday on a plan to transform six urban areas into parks designed to absorb rainwater, along with permeable pavements and rain gardens in several neighbourhoods. If approved, work is to begin in March, with the first park expected to open within eighteen months.

The plan comes after a series of floods last year left thousands of residents temporarily homeless. "We were on the verge of losing an entire neighbourhood," said the mayor at a press conference on Monday. "If we are to protect our citizens, we cannot simply build higher walls. We need to work with nature, not against it."

The concept of the "sponge city" was popularized in China, where cities have used green spaces, wetlands and permeable surfaces to reduce flooding. Experts say similar approaches are poised to spread across Latin America as extreme rainfall becomes more common.

Not everyone is convinced. Some business owners have warned that construction work is bound to disrupt trade in the city centre, while opposition councillors have questioned the project's estimated cost of 180 million reais.

Environmental scientist Dr. Helena Prado, who advised the council, said the investment would pay for itself. "Every flood costs the city millions in repairs and lost income," she explained. "The real question is not whether we can afford to do this, but whether we can afford not to."

The council's decision is expected to be announced on Tuesday evening.

grammar.title: Multi-word verbs with abstract meanings
grammar.explanation_pt:
Muitos phrasal verbs têm um **sentido literal** (B1/B2) e um **sentido abstrato** (C1), que aparece em textos formais.

**1. Causa e origem:**
- **bring about** = causar, provocar (mudança): "The war **brought about** mass migration."
- **stem from** = originar-se de: "Many problems **stem from** a lack of documents."
- **give rise to** = dar origem a: "Climate change **gives rise to** new forms of displacement."
- **lead to / result in** (revisão)

**2. Explicar e quantificar:**
- **account for** = representar (proporção) / explicar: "Women **account for** half of all migrants." / "How do you **account for** the increase?"
- **bear out** = confirmar: "The data **bear out** this theory."
- **point to** = indicar: "Studies **point to** economic factors."

**3. Enfrentar e lidar:**
- **come up against** = deparar-se com (obstáculo)
- **face up to** = encarar (realidade difícil)
- **grapple / contend with** = lutar com, lidar com
- **cope with / deal with** (revisão)

**4. Começar, propor-se, eliminar:**
- **set out to** = propor-se a / **set up** = criar, estabelecer
- **embark on** = embarcar em, começar (projeto, jornada)
- **do away with** = abolir / **phase out** = eliminar gradualmente
- **draw up** = elaborar (plano, documento) / **carry out** = realizar

**5. Outros úteis:**
- **fall through** = fracassar (plano) · **put forward** = propor (ideia) · **rule out** = descartar · **look into** = investigar · **bring up** = mencionar · **step up** = intensificar

**Registro:** muitos phrasal verbs têm equivalentes latinos mais formais:
bring about = **cause** · set up = **establish** · look into = **investigate** · do away with = **abolish** · put forward = **propose** · rule out = **exclude**
Em redações C1, uma **mistura** dos dois soa natural; só latinos soa pesado.

**Gramática:** verbos de três partes são **inseparáveis**: "face up **to** it" (não "face it up to").

rows: We must face up to the facts.
They did away with the visa.

examples.en: Much of the hostility towards migrants stems from misinformation about their impact on jobs and public services.
examples.pt: Grande parte da hostilidade contra migrantes vem da desinformação sobre seu impacto nos empregos e serviços públicos.

examples.en: Many newly arrived refugees come up against language barriers, bureaucracy and, at times, open prejudice.
examples.pt: Muitos refugiados recém-chegados esbarram em barreiras linguísticas, burocracia e, às vezes, preconceito aberto.

examples.en: Remittances account for a significant share of the economy in several Latin American countries.
examples.pt: As remessas representam uma parcela significativa da economia em vários países latino-americanos.

grammar.tip_pt: **Account for** é muito útil e muito confundido: "Migrants **account for** 10% of the population" (= representam) / "This **accounts for** the rise" (= explica). Não confunda com "count" ou "represent for".

common_mistakes.right: Migrants account for 10% of the workforce.

common_mistakes.wrong: We must face the problem up to.
common_mistakes.right: We must face up to the problem.
common_mistakes.why_pt: Verbos de três partes não se separam.

pronunciation.tip_pt: Em phrasal verbs, o acento costuma cair na **partícula**: bring a**BOUT**, set **UP**, rule **OUT**. Em verbos de três partes, acento na **segunda** palavra: come up a**GAINST**? Não — come **UP** against, face **UP** to, do a**WAY** with.
practice: We must face UP to it.
They did aWAY with the rule.

dialogue.title: Starting again
dialogue.context_pt: Uma jornalista entrevista um homem venezuelano que reconstruiu a vida em Roraima e depois em Curitiba.

lines.speaker: Journalist
lines.en: Thank you for talking to us, Diego. What brought about your decision to leave Venezuela?
lines.pt: Obrigada por conversar conosco, Diego. O que provocou sua decisão de sair da Venezuela?

lines.speaker: Diego
lines.en: It stemmed from many things — shortages, no medicine for my mother, no future for my children. In the end, we simply couldn't cope with it any more.
lines.pt: Veio de muitas coisas — escassez, falta de remédio para minha mãe, nenhum futuro para meus filhos. No fim, simplesmente não conseguíamos mais lidar com aquilo.

lines.speaker: Journalist
lines.en: What were the first months in Brazil like?
lines.pt: Como foram os primeiros meses no Brasil?

lines.speaker: Diego
lines.en: Hard. We came up against so many obstacles — the language, documents, finding work. I'm an engineer, but at first I worked in a supermarket.
lines.pt: Difíceis. Esbarramos em muitos obstáculos — a língua, documentos, achar trabalho. Sou engenheiro, mas no começo trabalhei num supermercado.

lines.speaker: Journalist
lines.en: And how did you end up in Curitiba?
lines.pt: E como você acabou em Curitiba?

lines.speaker: Diego
lines.en: Through a relocation programme that helps people move from the border to other cities with more jobs. A local NGO helped us set up our life here.
lines.pt: Por meio de um programa de interiorização que ajuda pessoas a se mudarem da fronteira para outras cidades com mais empregos. Uma ONG local nos ajudou a montar nossa vida aqui.

lines.speaker: Journalist
lines.en: And now?
lines.pt: E agora?

lines.speaker: Diego
lines.en: I had my qualifications recognized last year, and I'm working as an engineer again. And I've set out to help other newcomers — I give free Portuguese classes on Saturdays.
lines.pt: Tive meu diploma reconhecido ano passado e estou trabalhando como engenheiro de novo. E me propus a ajudar outros recém-chegados — dou aulas gratuitas de português aos sábados.

lines.speaker: Journalist
lines.en: What would you say to Brazilians who are suspicious of migrants?
lines.pt: O que você diria aos brasileiros que desconfiam dos migrantes?

lines.speaker: Diego
lines.en: That most of that fear stems from not knowing us. Come and have a coffee with us. Most of us just want to work and give something back.
lines.pt: Que a maior parte desse medo vem de não nos conhecer. Venham tomar um café com a gente. A maioria de nós só quer trabalhar e retribuir.

listening.title: A nation of migrants
listening.context_pt: Um historiador fala sobre a história da migração no Brasil.

lines.speaker: Historian
lines.en: Brazil has been shaped by migration — much of it forced. Over three centuries, an estimated four to five million enslaved Africans were brought to Brazil, more than to any other country in the Americas. Their descendants account for a large part of today's population, and African influences run through Brazilian culture, from music and religion to food and language. From the late nineteenth century, a new wave of immigration began, much of it brought about by government policies to attract European labour after the abolition of slavery in 1888. Italians, Portuguese, Spaniards and Germans arrived in large numbers, followed by Japanese immigrants from 1908 — today, Brazil is home to the largest population of Japanese descent outside Japan. Lebanese and Syrian communities also set down deep roots. In recent decades, the picture has changed again: Brazil has received people from Haiti, Venezuela, Bolivia and African countries, while hundreds of thousands of Brazilians have themselves emigrated, to places such as the United States, Portugal and Japan.

questions.q: How many enslaved Africans were brought to Brazil, according to estimates?
questions.answer: Four to five million.

questions.q: What brought about the wave of European immigration?
questions.answer: Government policies to attract European labour after the abolition of slavery in 1888.

questions.q: What is notable about the Japanese community in Brazil?
questions.answer: It's the largest population of Japanese descent outside Japan.

questions.q: Where have many Brazilians emigrated to?
questions.answer: The United States, Portugal and Japan.

reading.title: The economics of migration
reading.text: Few issues provoke as much political debate as migration, and few are as widely misunderstood. Public opinion surveys in many countries suggest that people tend to overestimate the number of immigrants living among them, sometimes considerably. Much of the anxiety surrounding migration stems from economic fears: that newcomers will take jobs, push down wages or place an unbearable burden on public services. What does the evidence say? On the question of jobs, most economic research has failed to bear out the most pessimistic predictions. Migrants often take up work that local workers are unwilling or unavailable to do, or set up businesses that create new employment. Their effect on average wages is generally found to be small, although some studies point to modest negative effects for specific groups of low-skilled workers, particularly in the short term. Migrants also tend to be of working age, which means that, in ageing societies, they can help to pay for pensions and healthcare. At the same time, it would be naive to rule out real challenges. Rapid arrivals can put pressure on housing, schools and health services in particular areas, especially when governments fail to plan or invest accordingly. Integration does not happen automatically: newcomers frequently come up against language barriers, unrecognized qualifications and discrimination, all of which can prevent them from contributing fully. Emigration, meanwhile, has its own consequences for countries of origin. The "brain drain" of doctors, engineers and other professionals can weaken health and education systems, although remittances sent home by migrants account for a substantial share of income in many developing economies. Ultimately, the evidence suggests that migration is neither the catastrophe some fear nor the simple solution others claim. Its effects depend largely on how societies choose to face up to it.

questions.q: What do people tend to overestimate?
questions.answer: The number of immigrants living among them.

questions.q: What does most research say about migrants and jobs?

writing.model:
Proposal: The "Welcome Neighbour" integration programme

Introduction
The aim of this proposal is to put forward a programme to help the growing number of migrants and refugees in our city to integrate more quickly and fully into local life. Over the past five years, newcomers from Venezuela, Haiti and several African countries have come to account for a visible share of our population, yet support services remain limited.

Current situation
Interviews carried out by our association with more than sixty migrant families suggest that most of their difficulties stem from three sources: language barriers, the slow recognition of professional qualifications and a lack of information about public services. Many highly qualified people, including nurses and engineers, come up against so much bureaucracy that they end up in low-paid, informal work. This represents a waste of talent that the city cannot afford.

Proposal
We propose that the council set up a "Welcome Neighbour" centre, run in partnership with local NGOs and universities. The centre would:
• offer free Portuguese classes at different levels, including evening and weekend options;
• help newcomers draw up the documents needed to have their qualifications recognized;
• pair each family with a local volunteer "neighbour" for their first six months;
• organize regular cultural events to bring migrant and local communities together.

Expected benefits
The programme is likely to bring about faster integration into the job market, which would in turn increase tax revenue and reduce dependence on social support. Perhaps more importantly, it would help to do away with the misunderstandings and prejudice that often arise when communities live side by side without meeting.

Conclusion
We are aware that the council is facing budget constraints. However, the costs of the programme would be modest, and we believe the city cannot afford to ignore the issue. We would welcome the opportunity to present the proposal in more detail.

grammar.title: Distancing language
grammar.explanation_pt:
**1. Advérbios de distanciamento** — mostram que a informação **não foi confirmada** pelo autor:
- **allegedly** (acusação ainda não provada): "The mayor **allegedly** used public funds."
- **reportedly** (segundo relatos/a imprensa): "The singer is **reportedly** planning a tour."
- **supposedly** (supostamente — com dúvida/ironia): "The diet **supposedly** cures everything."
- **apparently** (ao que parece), **purportedly** (formal, = supostamente), **ostensibly** (aparentemente, mas na verdade não)

**2. Passivas de relato** (revisão B2 + todos os tempos):
- **It is + particípio + that**: "**It is alleged that** he lied." / "**It has been reported that**..."
- **Sujeito + be + particípio + infinitivo**:
  • presente: "He **is said to be** in Portugal."
  • contínuo: "He **is thought to be hiding** abroad."
  • passado: "He **is alleged to have lied**."
  • passado passivo: "The data **are believed to have been manipulated**."
  • passado do relato: "She **was reported to have left** the country."
- **There is said / thought to be**: "**There are thought to be** thousands of fake accounts."

**3. Reporting verbs que mostram atitude:**
- **Neutro:** say, state, report, explain
- **Dúvida do autor:** **claim** (afirmar, sem prova), **allege**, **purport**
- **Admitir:** **admit**, **concede** (admitir a contragosto), **acknowledge**
- **Negar:** **deny** (+ -ing / that), **reject**, **dismiss** (descartar como sem importância)
- **Insistir:** **insist**, **maintain** (sustentar), **assert**
- **Prometer/ameaçar:** pledge, vow, threaten

Compare: "The CEO **said** profits were stable" (neutro) x "The CEO **claimed** profits were stable" (o jornalista duvida) x "The CEO **conceded** profits had fallen" (admitiu a contragosto).

listening.title: Why lies spread faster
listening.context_pt: Uma pesquisadora fala sobre um estudo famoso sobre notícias falsas no Twitter.

lines.speaker: Researcher
lines.en: In 2018, a team of researchers at MIT published a study in the journal Science that analysed around 126,000 stories shared on Twitter between 2006 and 2017. Each story had been checked by independent fact-checking organizations. The findings were striking. False stories were found to spread significantly further, faster and more widely than true ones. According to the study, false news was about 70 percent more likely to be retweeted than the truth. Why? The researchers suggested that false stories tend to be more novel and surprising, and that they provoke stronger emotional reactions, such as disgust and fear. Interestingly, the study concluded that it was humans, not automated bots, who were primarily responsible for the difference. Bots were found to spread true and false stories at similar rates. The implication is uncomfortable. If we want to fight misinformation, it is not enough to blame algorithms or foreign agents. We also have to look at our own behaviour — and pause before we click "share".

questions.answer: About 70 percent more likely.

questions.q: Why do false stories spread faster, according to the researchers?
questions.answer: They are more novel and provoke stronger emotions.

questions.q: Who was primarily responsible for spreading false news?
questions.answer: Humans, not bots.

reading.title: The age of deepfakes
reading.text: In 2018, a video appeared online in which former US president Barack Obama seemed to insult his successor. The video was not real. It had been created by the media company BuzzFeed, in collaboration with the filmmaker Jordan Peele, who voiced the words, to warn the public about a new kind of technology: deepfakes. Since then, the tools needed to produce convincing fake video and audio have become dramatically cheaper and easier to use. What once required a professional studio can now reportedly be done in minutes with a laptop or even a phone. The consequences are already visible. Fake audio recordings of politicians have allegedly been circulated shortly before elections in several countries, when there is little time to debunk them. Criminals are reported to have used cloned voices of company executives to persuade employees to transfer money. Ordinary people, too, have been targeted with fabricated images. Perhaps the most worrying effect, however, is not that people will believe fake content but that they will stop believing real content. Researchers have called this the "liar's dividend": when anything could be fake, those caught on camera doing something wrong can simply claim that the evidence has been fabricated. Truth itself becomes a matter of opinion. There are responses. Technology companies are said to be developing tools to detect manipulated media and to label AI-generated content, and several governments have introduced or proposed regulations. Journalists and fact-checkers are increasingly trained in verification techniques. But most experts concede that technology alone cannot solve the problem. In the end, the best defence may be an old-fashioned one: a healthy scepticism, combined with trust in reliable, accountable sources.

questions.answer: To warn the public about deepfake technology.

questions.q: How have criminals reportedly used deepfakes?
questions.answer: Cloned voices of executives to persuade employees to transfer money.

questions.q: What is the "liar's dividend"?
questions.answer: When anything could be fake, people caught doing wrong can claim the evidence was fabricated.

questions.q: What may be the best defence, according to the text?
questions.answer: Healthy scepticism combined with trust in reliable, accountable sources.

writing.model:
Health app accused of selling users' data

A popular fitness app with more than five million Brazilian users is alleged to have sold sensitive health information to advertisers without users' consent, according to an investigation published yesterday. (Fictional story created for this lesson.)

The company, VidaFit, reportedly shared data including users' weight, sleep patterns and menstrual cycles with at least three marketing firms between 2022 and 2024. Internal emails seen by journalists are said to show that senior managers were aware of the practice.

In a statement released on Monday evening, VidaFit's CEO, Marcos Teixeira, denied that the company had "ever sold personal data". He insisted that all information shared with partners had been "fully anonymized" and claimed that users had agreed to the practice when accepting the app's terms and conditions.

Privacy experts, however, dismissed this explanation. "Health data is extremely difficult to anonymize," said Dr. Larissa Moura, a specialist in digital rights. "And it is hard to argue that consent buried on page forty of the terms is genuine consent."

The national data protection authority is understood to have opened a preliminary investigation. If the allegations are confirmed, the company could face fines of up to 2% of its revenue in Brazil, as provided for under the General Data Protection Law (LGPD).

By Tuesday afternoon, the company appeared to be changing its position. A spokesperson conceded that "communication with users could have been clearer" and announced that the data-sharing programme had been suspended "as a precaution".

The case has prompted calls for stricter rules on health apps. Thousands of users are thought to have deleted their accounts since the story broke, and a consumer group has threatened to take legal action.

grammar.title: Cohesion in writing
grammar.explanation_pt:
**Coesão** = os mecanismos que **ligam** frases e parágrafos. Um texto C1 usa vários, **sem exagerar nos conectores**.

**1. Referência (para trás):**
- **this / that / these / those** + substantivo: "Many cities have introduced bike lanes. **This policy** has..."
- **such** + substantivo (= desse tipo): "**Such measures** are expensive." / "**Such a policy**..."
- **the former / the latter** (o primeiro / o último de **dois**): "Investing in schools or hospitals? **The former** has long-term benefits; **the latter** saves lives now."
- **it / they / which** (pronomes — cuidado com ambiguidade!)

**2. "Umbrella nouns"** — substantivos gerais que resumem uma ideia anterior:
**this issue / problem / trend / approach / development / situation / view / claim / argument / measure / phenomenon**
"Young people are increasingly leaving rural areas. **This trend** has serious consequences..."

**3. Sinônimos e variação lexical** — evite repetir a mesma palavra:
public transport → the transport network → buses and trains → the system

**4. Substituição e elipse** (revisão C1-M1-L2): do so, one(s), so/not.

**5. Transições entre parágrafos** (ligam ideia anterior + nova):
- "**Turning now to** healthcare, ..."
- "**Another area which deserves attention is**..."
- "**While** improving transport would clearly benefit commuters, **investing in** education might have more far-reaching effects."
- "**Having considered** X, **it is worth examining** Y."

**6. Estrutura do essay C1 Advanced (avaliar 2 de 3 opções):**
1. **Introdução:** apresente o tema e diga quais duas opções vai discutir.
2. **Parágrafo 1:** opção A — vantagens, exemplos, possíveis limitações.
3. **Parágrafo 2:** opção B — idem.
4. **Conclusão:** diga **qual é mais importante/eficaz** e **por quê** (obrigatório!).

⚠️ **Dica:** um conector por frase é muito. Use **referência e vocabulário** para criar coesão — isso é o que distingue C1.

pronunciation.tip_pt: **Former** = "FÓR-mer" e **latter** = "LÉ-ter" (no americano, o tt soa quase como um "r" rápido: "LÉ-rer"). Não confunda **latter** (o último) com **later** ("LÊI-ter", mais tarde)!
practice: Of the two, the former is cheaper.

dialogue.title: Exam preparation
dialogue.context_pt: Uma professora e uma aluna analisam juntas o planejamento de um essay C1 Advanced.

lines.speaker: Teacher
lines.en: OK, the task: your class has discussed three ways governments could improve quality of life in cities — public transport, green spaces and affordable housing. You have to discuss two and say which is more important.
lines.pt: OK, a tarefa: sua turma discutiu três formas de os governos melhorarem a qualidade de vida nas cidades — transporte público, áreas verdes e moradia acessível. Você precisa discutir duas e dizer qual é mais importante.

lines.speaker: Luiza
lines.en: I'll choose transport and housing. I have more ideas for those.
lines.pt: Vou escolher transporte e moradia. Tenho mais ideias para essas.

lines.speaker: Teacher
lines.en: Good strategy. Now, look at your draft. You wrote "public transport" seven times in one paragraph.
lines.pt: Boa estratégia. Agora, olhe seu rascunho. Você escreveu "public transport" sete vezes num parágrafo.

lines.speaker: Luiza
lines.en: I know. I didn't know how to avoid it.
lines.pt: Eu sei. Não sabia como evitar.

lines.speaker: Teacher
lines.en: Use reference and synonyms. After the first mention, try "the transport network", "buses and trains" or "this investment".
lines.pt: Use referência e sinônimos. Depois da primeira menção, tente "the transport network", "buses and trains" ou "this investment".

lines.speaker: Luiza
lines.en: And here? "Building houses is good. Building houses is expensive."
lines.pt: E aqui? "Construir casas é bom. Construir casas é caro."

lines.speaker: Teacher
lines.en: Combine them with an umbrella noun: "Building affordable homes would benefit millions. Such a programme, however, would be costly."
lines.pt: Combine com um umbrella noun: "Construir moradias acessíveis beneficiaria milhões. Um programa desse tipo, porém, seria caro."

lines.speaker: Luiza
lines.en: That sounds much better. And in the conclusion, I can say "Of the two, the latter is more urgent"?
lines.pt: Fica bem melhor. E na conclusão, posso dizer "Das duas, a última é mais urgente"?

lines.speaker: Teacher
lines.en: Perfect — as long as it's clear which one is "the latter". And remember: you must say which is more important and why. Many students forget that.
lines.pt: Perfeito — desde que fique claro qual é "a última". E lembre-se: você precisa dizer qual é mais importante e por quê. Muitos alunos esquecem.

listening.title: What examiners look for
listening.context_pt: Uma examinadora explica os critérios de correção do essay C1.

lines.speaker: Examiner
lines.en: At C1 level, the difference between a good essay and an excellent one is often not the ideas but the organization. We assess writing in four areas: content, communicative achievement, organization and language. Under organization, we're looking for a text that is well structured and cohesive, using a variety of devices — not just linking words. Many candidates think that the more "furthermore" and "moreover" they use, the higher their score will be. In fact, overusing linking words can make a text feel mechanical. What really impresses examiners is when ideas flow naturally: when a sentence refers back to the previous one using "this problem" or "such an approach", and when paragraphs are connected by a clear line of argument. The other common mistake is forgetting part of the task. In the essay, you must clearly state which option you consider more important, and give reasons. If you don't, your content score will suffer, however good your English is.

questions.q: What is often the difference between good and excellent essays at C1?
questions.answer: The organization, not the ideas.

questions.q: What mistake do many candidates make with linking words?
questions.answer: They overuse them, making the text feel mechanical.

questions.q: What really impresses examiners?
questions.answer: Ideas flowing naturally, with reference (this problem, such an approach) and a clear line of argument.

questions.q: What part of the task do candidates often forget?
questions.answer: Stating which option is more important and giving reasons.

reading.title: Model essay: Improving life in cities
reading.text:
Over half of the world's population now lives in cities, and this proportion is expected to keep rising. As a result, the question of how to make urban life healthier and more sustainable has become increasingly urgent. Of the various measures available to governments, investment in public transport and the provision of affordable housing are two of the most frequently discussed.

An efficient public transport system can transform daily life. When buses and trains are frequent, safe and affordable, fewer people depend on cars, which in turn reduces congestion, air pollution and carbon emissions. Such a network also widens access to jobs and education, particularly for those living on the outskirts. However, this kind of infrastructure is costly and can take years to build, and its benefits depend heavily on good planning and maintenance.

Affordable housing, by contrast, addresses a more fundamental need. In many cities, soaring rents have pushed low-income families into informal settlements or distant suburbs, where they face long commutes and limited services. Providing decent homes closer to city centres would not only improve living conditions but also reduce the very travel demands that transport investment seeks to meet. Admittedly, such programmes can be poorly managed and may concentrate poverty if they are badly designed.

On balance, although both measures are valuable, I believe the latter should be the priority. Without a secure, affordable place to live, people cannot fully benefit from any other improvement a city has to offer. Moreover, well-located housing reduces the need for long journeys in the first place, making it, in the long term, the more far-reaching solution.

questions.q: Which two measures does the essay discuss?
questions.answer: Investment in public transport and affordable housing.

questions.q: What benefits of public transport are mentioned?
questions.answer: Less congestion, pollution and emissions; wider access to jobs and education.

questions.q: Find two examples of cohesive devices in paragraph 2.
questions.answer: Such a network / this kind of infrastructure / which in turn / However.

questions.q: Which option does the writer prioritize, and why?
questions.answer: Affordable housing (the latter): it's a fundamental need and reduces the need for long journeys.

exercises.title: Umbrella nouns
exercises.instruction: Complete with: trend · measure · issue · approach · development.
exercises.instruction_pt: Complete com o umbrella noun adequado.

items.prompt: More and more young people are moving abroad. This ___ worries economists.
The city banned cars from the centre on Sundays. This ___ proved very popular.
Some schools teach through projects instead of exams. This ___ encourages creativity.
Housing costs have doubled. This ___ must be addressed. Recently, a new metro line opened — a welcome ___.
Governments can tax sugar or ban advertising. ___ raises money; the latter changes habits.

exercises.title: Improve cohesion
exercises.instruction: Rewrite the pairs of sentences to avoid repetition, using reference, umbrella nouns or synonyms.
exercises.instruction_pt: Reescreva os pares de frases evitando repetição.

items.prompt: Many cities offer free public transport. Free public transport reduces traffic.
items.answer: Many cities offer free public transport. Such schemes reduce traffic. / This measure reduces traffic.

items.prompt: Older people are often isolated. Older people need more support.
items.answer: Older people are often isolated. Senior citizens / They need more support.

items.prompt: Governments could raise taxes or cut spending. Raising taxes is unpopular. Cutting spending affects services.
items.answer: Governments could raise taxes or cut spending. The former is unpopular, while the latter affects services.
The former is cheaper; the latter is faster.
On balance, I believe that housing should be the priority.

items.prompt: Such policy would be popular.
items.answer: Such a policy would be popular. / Such policies would be popular.

items.prompt: We discussed transport, housing and parks. The latter is the most important.
items.answer: We discussed transport, housing and parks. The last is the most important. / Parks are the most important.

items.prompt: I'll discuss this issue latter in the essay.
items.answer: I'll discuss this issue later in the essay.

items.prompt: In other hand, this trend has advantages.
items.answer: On the other hand, this trend has advantages.

exercises.title: Plan the essay
exercises.instruction: Put the parts of a C1 essay in the correct order (write the letters).
exercises.instruction_pt: Coloque as partes do essay C1 na ordem correta (escreva as letras).

items.prompt: a) Affordable housing, by contrast, addresses... / b) On balance, I believe the latter should be the priority... / c) Over half of the world's population lives in cities... This essay will consider... / d) An efficient public transport system can transform daily life...

speaking.instruction: "Budget committee": your group has money for only one of three projects in your city (a new metro line, a social housing programme, a network of parks). Discuss two in detail, compare them using the former / the latter, and agree on a final recommendation.
speaking.instruction_pt: "Comitê de orçamento": o grupo tem verba para apenas um de três projetos na cidade (nova linha de metrô, programa de moradia social, rede de parques). Discutam dois em detalhe, comparem usando the former / the latter e cheguem a uma recomendação final.
questions: Which public policy would most improve life in your city?
Should governments prioritize short-term or long-term solutions?
Is it better to invest in education or in healthcare? Why?
How should public money be allocated: by experts or by citizens?
What policy from another country would you like Brazil to adopt?

writing.task: C1 Advanced essay (220–260 words): "Your class has discussed three ways governments could reduce inequality: free university education, a guaranteed minimum income, and investment in early childhood education. Write an essay discussing two of these, explaining which is more effective and why." Use a range of cohesive devices.
writing.task_pt: Essay C1 Advanced (220–260 palavras): "Sua turma discutiu três formas de os governos reduzirem a desigualdade: universidade gratuita, renda mínima garantida e investimento na educação infantil. Discuta duas delas, explicando qual é mais eficaz e por quê." Use vários recursos de coesão.
writing.model:
Reducing inequality: where should governments begin?

Inequality remains one of the most persistent challenges facing countries such as Brazil. Of the many policies proposed to address this issue, a guaranteed minimum income and investment in early childhood education are among the most widely debated.

A guaranteed minimum income offers immediate relief. By ensuring that every household has enough to cover its basic needs, such a scheme can reduce extreme poverty almost overnight. Cash transfer programmes have been credited with lowering poverty rates in several countries, including Brazil, and they allow families to decide for themselves how best to spend the money. Nevertheless, this approach is expensive and, on its own, does little to change the conditions that cause poverty in the first place.

Early childhood education, by contrast, targets those underlying conditions. Research suggests that the first years of life are crucial for cognitive and social development, and that children from poorer families who attend high-quality nurseries and pre-schools are more likely to succeed later on. The benefits of this investment, however, take many years to appear, which makes it politically less attractive.

On balance, although both measures have clear merits, I believe the latter is ultimately more effective. While a minimum income alleviates the symptoms of inequality, early education addresses one of its root causes, giving children a fairer start regardless of their background. Ideally, the two policies would work together; if only one can be prioritized, however, investing in the youngest citizens is likely to have the most far-reaching impact.

culture_note.title: Coesão em inglês x português
culture_note.text_pt: Textos acadêmicos em português costumam aceitar frases longas, com muitas orações subordinadas. Em inglês, a tradição valoriza frases mais **curtas e diretas**, ligadas por **referência** (this, such, these) em vez de conectores longos. Uma dica prática: se sua frase em inglês tem mais de 35 palavras, provavelmente vale dividir em duas.

summary_pt: Referência: this / these + umbrella noun; such (a) + noun.
the former / the latter: só para dois itens.
Sinônimos e variação evitam repetição; menos conectores, mais referência.
Essay C1: introdução · opção A · opção B · conclusão com qual é mais importante e por quê.

review.intro_pt: Revise futuro formal, multi-word verbs abstratos, linguagem de distanciamento e coesão.

items.prompt: Food prices are set ___ rise again.
The species is on the brink ___ extinction.
The problem stems ___ a lack of investment.
The suspect is believed ___ the country.
___ measures have been introduced in other countries.
If we want to succeed, we must cooperate. (If we are to...)
items.answer: If we are to succeed, we must cooperate.

items.prompt: Migrants represent 10% of the workforce. (account)
items.answer: Migrants account for 10% of the workforce.

items.prompt: It is alleged that the mayor accepted bribes. (The mayor...)
items.answer: The mayor is alleged to have accepted bribes.

items.prompt: O relatório deve ser publicado na segunda (previsto).
items.answer: The report is due to be published on Monday.

items.prompt: Eles esbarraram em muita burocracia.
items.answer: They came up against a lot of bureaucracy.

items.prompt: A primeira opção é mais barata; a segunda é mais rápida.
items.answer: The former is cheaper; the latter is faster.
The summit is to be held in Belém.
The war brought about a huge wave of migration.
She conceded that mistakes had been made.

items.prompt: The forest is on the verge to collapse.
items.answer: The forest is on the verge of collapse / of collapsing.

items.prompt: He is said that he is very rich.
items.answer: He is said to be very rich.

items.prompt: Such policy would be unpopular.
items.answer: Such a policy would be unpopular.

review.speaking_pt: Faça uma apresentação de 5 minutos no formato "policy briefing" sobre uma questão global (clima, migração ou desinformação): apresente previsões (futuro formal), explique causas e consequências (multi-word verbs), relate informações com distanciamento e termine com uma recomendação bem argumentada (coesão).
speaking_questions: Which global issue will define the next decade?
Can individuals make a real difference to global problems?
How should Brazil respond to climate migration?
Who is responsible for stopping misinformation?
If you could change one global policy, what would it be?
review.project_pt: **"Model UN":** a turma simula uma sessão da ONU sobre uma questão global. Cada grupo representa um país, prepara um discurso de 2 minutos (com futuro formal e distanciamento), negocia com os outros e, no final, todos redigem juntos uma resolução de 300 palavras, coesa e formal.
